core_obligations: Choose representatives (proof lines 9065-9068): take a K-flat complex K^bullet representing K, a K-injective complex I^bullet representing L, and any complex M^bullet representing M.

Resolve the tensor product injectively (proof lines 9068-9071): choose a quasi-isomorphism Tot(K^bullet tensor I^bullet) -> J^bullet with J^bullet K-injective, so that the target can be read as an internal hom into a K-injective complex.

Build the chain of maps (proof lines 9071-9082): Tot(K^bullet tensor SheafHom^bullet(M^bullet, I^bullet)) -> SheafHom^bullet(M^bullet, Tot(K^bullet tensor I^bullet)) -> SheafHom^bullet(M^bullet, J^bullet), where the first map is the one supplied by the cited same-chapter lemma.
Conclude (proof lines 9047-9083): the source represents K tensor^L RSheafHom(M, L) and the target represents RSheafHom(M, K tensor^L L), so the composite is the asserted canonical morphism.
proof_roadmap: Represent K by a K-flat complex, L by a K-injective complex, and resolve Tot(K tensor I) by a K-injective J.
Take the first arrow from the earlier same-chapter lemma on the diagonal map.
Post-compose with the map induced by the quasi-isomorphism into J.
Read the source and target as the two derived objects of the statement.
difficulty_reason: The lemma constructs the canonical map K tensor^L RSheafHom(M, L) -> RSheafHom(M, K tensor^L L) on the derived category of a ringed site (statement lines 9052-9062). The construction requires two independent resolution choices: K is represented by a K-flat complex so that the derived tensor product is computed by the naive one, and the tensor product K tensor^L I is resolved by a K-injective J so that the target internal hom can be evaluated at all (proof lines 9065-9071). Only then can the first arrow be taken from the earlier diagonal lemma and composed with the arrow induced by the quasi-isomorphism (proof lines 9071-9083). The claim is H2: one construction whose only non-formal content is the choice of resolutions and the recognition of the two represented objects.
